children: Crude oil prices tumbled below $100 a barrel on Friday, erasing gains after a volatile session and falling for a third consecutive session.
Markets expect the closure of Saudi Arabia’s key pipeline to have a smaller impact on supplies than initially feared.

Satellite imagery suggests Saudi Arabia moved 2.8 million bpd through the Strait of Hormuz over the past six days, compared with just 700,000 bpd in August. Saudi Arabia has reportedly sold as many as 60 million barrels of crude from the Persian Gulf port of Ras Tanura for September and October loadings outside the strait through ship-to-ship transfers.
Reports that Aramco expects to restore half of the pipeline’s daily flows also eased supply concerns.
Still, only four commodity vessels were detected moving through Hormuz on Thursday.
Volumes from Hormuz are being picked up mostly by refiners in China and South Korea.
China exported 6.01 million tons of refined fuels in August, up 12.7% yearly.
Oil prices fell 0.5% on the week.

title: Oil Falls Below $100 as Supply Fears Ease
